lessons.title: Finding Your Way Around Setup and Maintenance
lessons.chapterTitle: Getting Started in the Practice Environment

slots.practicalActivity: Activate your Oracle Fusion practice environment, sign in, and open the Setup and Maintenance work area. Search for and open at least 5 different setup tasks by name (for example "Manage Legal Entity", "Manage Ledgers", "Manage Chart of Accounts Structures") just to see where each one lives, without changing anything yet, and note which functional area (offering) each task is filed under.
slots.deliverable: A short list (task name -> offering/functional area) for the 5 setup tasks you located, plus a one-line note on how Setup and Maintenance's search differs from browsing by offering.

lessons.title: Enterprise Structures Overview
lessons.chapterTitle: Getting Started in the Practice Environment

lessons.title: Functional Setup Manager and Task Lists
lessons.chapterTitle: Getting Started in the Practice Environment

slots.practicalActivity: In the practice environment, open Functional Setup Manager and locate the implementation task list for the Financials offering. Walk through the task list's hierarchy (offering -> functional area -> task) and identify, without clicking Go Live on anything, which 4-5 tasks correspond to the enterprise structure components this course covers: legal entities, ledgers, business units, and chart of accounts.
slots.deliverable: A simple outline (copied into your own notes) mapping the Financials offering's task list down to the specific tasks for legal entities, ledgers, business units, and chart of accounts.

lessons.title: Legal Entities and Legal Reporting Units

slots.practicalActivity: Using the Manage Legal Address task, create a legal address for a fictional US entity. Then use Manage Legal Entity to register a legal entity against that address with an identifying jurisdiction (United States Income Tax) and registration number, and confirm Oracle Fusion auto-creates a matching legal reporting unit. Finally open Manage Ledgers and inspect an existing primary ledger's four required components (chart of accounts, calendar, currency, accounting method) without changing them, so you can see why they lock once saved.
slots.deliverable: A registered legal entity (with its auto-created legal reporting unit) in the practice environment, plus written notes identifying the four locked components of the ledger you inspected.

slots.practicalActivity: Group two ledgers that share the same chart of accounts and calendar into a single ledger set, and confirm it opens journals/reports across both at once rather than storing its own balances. Then run the Accounting Configuration Manager end to end for a new primary ledger definition, stepping through legal entity assignment, chart of accounts assignment, calendar, and currency in the order the wizard presents them.
slots.deliverable: One configured ledger set containing two compatible ledgers, plus a completed (not yet live) ledger definition walked through Accounting Configuration Manager.

slots.practicalActivity: Define two business units for the same legal entity (for example East Region Sales and West Region Sales), assign each to the same primary ledger, and turn on at least one business function (such as Requisitioning or Payables Invoicing) per unit so they're not interchangeable. Then create a reference data set and assign it to one of the business units, leaving the other on the Common set, so you can see the difference in practice.
slots.deliverable: Two business units under one legal entity with distinct business functions assigned, plus one custom reference data set attached to only one of them.

slots.practicalActivity: List three reference data types (such as payment terms, tax rules, and transaction types) and decide, for each, whether it should be shared (Common set) or non-shared (business-unit-specific) for your two business units from the previous slot, writing one sentence of justification per decision. Then use Manage Locations to create a physical location for one business unit and tie it to a geography already defined in the practice environment.
slots.deliverable: A short reference-data-sharing decision table (3 data types, shared or not, with justification) plus one new location record tied to a real geography.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a monthly (Gregorian) accounting calendar covering one fiscal year, naming each period clearly (Jan-26, Feb-26, and so on), and add a 13th adjusting period at year end for audit true-up entries. Then enable USD and GBP as currencies and define a Corporate conversion rate type for converting between them.
slots.deliverable: A complete 13-period accounting calendar (12 regular + 1 adjusting) plus USD/GBP enabled with a Corporate rate type defined.

slots.practicalActivity: Enter a daily GBP-to-USD conversion rate for the Corporate rate type on a specific date, then manually convert a sample 8,500 GBP amount using that rate to confirm your math matches what the system would compute. Finally, using the calendar you built, open the first accounting period of your fiscal year on the ledger from Slot 4, and confirm its status shows as Open.
slots.deliverable: One daily conversion rate entry with a hand-verified conversion calculation, plus a ledger with its first accounting period successfully opened.

lessons.title: Chart of Accounts Structure and Segments

slots.practicalActivity: Define a new chart of accounts structure with five segments (Company, Cost Center, Account, Intercompany, Future), choosing a segment width for each, before assigning any labels or values yet. Sketch out what a full account combination would look like under this structure, the same way the lesson's "110:400:6100:000" example does.
slots.deliverable: A saved (not yet frozen) 5-segment chart of accounts structure definition, plus a written example account combination showing one value per segment.

lessons.title: Segment Labels: Balancing, Cost Center and Natural Account

slots.practicalActivity: Assign the three mandatory-style segment labels to your 5-segment structure from the previous slot: Balancing (primary) on Company, Cost Center on Cost Center, and Natural Account on Account. Leave Intercompany and Future unlabeled or lightly labeled, then explain in writing why Oracle Fusion requires a balancing segment on every chart of accounts.
slots.deliverable: Your structure with Balancing, Cost Center, and Natural Account labels correctly assigned, plus a short written explanation of why the balancing segment is mandatory.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a value set for the Cost Center segment and populate it with at least 5 values (for example Assembly 410, Fabrication 420, Corporate Overhead 510, Sales 200, Admin 300). Then build a tree hierarchy that rolls those values up under two parent nodes ("Manufacturing" and "Corporate") so a report could total either grouping.
slots.deliverable: A Cost Center value set with 5+ values, plus a two-branch account hierarchy tree rolling those values up into Manufacturing and Corporate parents.

slots.practicalActivity: Write one cross-validation rule that blocks an invalid combination your business wouldn't allow in real life (for example, the Corporate Overhead cost center combined with a Cost of Goods Sold natural account range), using the hierarchy ranges from the previous slot rather than individual values. Deploy the rule and then deliberately try to enter an account combination that should fail it, confirming it's actually enforced.
slots.deliverable: One deployed cross-validation rule, plus a screenshot or written log of a deliberately invalid combination being rejected by it.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter lab: assemble the full Chart of Accounts picture end to end. Starting from your 5-segment structure, confirm every segment label, every value set, the account hierarchy, and the cross-validation rule from this chapter's lessons work together correctly by entering 3 sample account combinations: one that should be valid and post cleanly, one that should fail cross-validation, and one that should fail because a segment value doesn't exist in its value set.
slots.deliverable: A short test log of the 3 sample account combinations attempted, each with its expected outcome stated in advance and the actual outcome recorded.

lessons.title: Designing a Chart of Accounts for a Manufacturer

slots.practicalActivity: Work through the lesson's LTV Manufacturing Corporation scenario (two legal entities, three cost centers per entity, intercompany tracking) as your own rehearsal: write out your own five-segment design decision by decision, justifying why each segment got the label it did and why a Product Line segment was deliberately left out for now rather than built as an active segment.
slots.deliverable: A written chart-of-accounts design memo for LTV Manufacturing Corporation listing all 5 segments, their labels, their value ranges, and the one-sentence reason Product Line was excluded.

slots.practicalActivity: Freeze and deploy the LTV Manufacturing chart of accounts structure you designed in the previous slot, creating a structure instance tied to real value sets. Then download a Rapid Implementation spreadsheet template, populate it with a batch of chart of accounts values and a ledger definition for LTV Manufacturing, and upload it to load the setup in bulk instead of clicking through every screen by hand.
slots.deliverable: A deployed, usable chart of accounts structure instance for LTV Manufacturing, plus a completed Rapid Implementation spreadsheet used to bulk-load part of its setup.

lessons.title: Testing and Reviewing Your Enterprise Structure

slots.practicalActivity: Test the deployed LTV Manufacturing enterprise structure by entering one sample journal against it (one line per legal entity's Company value) and confirming it balances per balancing segment value, then review every setup task from this course against the finished structure (legal entities, ledgers, business units, calendar, currencies, chart of accounts) to confirm nothing was left half-configured.
slots.deliverable: One successfully entered and balanced test journal against the LTV Manufacturing structure, plus a completed setup review checklist covering all six enterprise structure components.

slots.practicalActivity: Audit your own LTV Manufacturing enterprise structure against the lesson's two mistake checklists (chart of accounts mistakes and ledger/legal entity mistakes), confirming specifically that a balancing segment value is assigned per legal entity and that your cross-validation rule was actually tested, not just deployed and forgotten.
slots.deliverable: A completed self-audit checklist against both mistake lists, with a pass/fail note and fix (if needed) for each item.

slots.practicalActivity: Capstone lab: starting from a blank practice environment task list, rebuild the entire LTV Manufacturing enterprise structure from scratch without re-reading the lessons first -- legal entities and addresses, a primary ledger with its four Cs, two business units, a calendar, enabled currencies, and the full 5-segment chart of accounts with labels, value sets, a hierarchy, and a cross-validation rule -- then re-run the Slot 13 test journal against your rebuilt structure to confirm it posts and balances correctly.
slots.deliverable: A fully rebuilt, independently assembled enterprise structure and chart of accounts for LTV Manufacturing, verified by one successfully posted and balanced test journal.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can design, configure, and deploy a complete Oracle Fusion enterprise structure from scratch -- legal entities, ledgers, business units, calendars, currencies, and a working chart of accounts with cross-validation rules -- the foundation every other Financials module in this path is built on.
